sections.h2: Plastic packaging recycled-content target rises from 30% to 60% by 2028-29

chart.title: Category I targets climb every year, from 30% to 60% of new packaging
chart.sub: Minimum recycled content in new plastic packaging, Category I, %.
chart.source: Plastic Waste Management (Amendment) Rules, 2026 (G.S.R. 237(E)); Corporate Professionals.

sections.means: The 2026 rules kept the 2022 recycled-content percentages, which now rise from 30% in 2025-26 to 60% from 2028-29.
sections.todo: Check whether CPCB has issued the recycled-content verification guidelines that were due by end-September 2026.

sections.h2: Battery recovery target rises from 70% to 90% in two years

chart.title: Battery manufacturers must recover 90% of materials by 2026-27, up from 70%
chart.sub: Battery-material recovery rate required of manufacturers, %.
chart.source: CSE policy brief, 2026; Battery Waste Management Rules.

sections.means: Under the Battery Waste Management Rules, manufacturers must lift material recovery from 70% in 2024-25 to 90% by 2026-27.
sections.todo: Track how many batteries registered recyclers can physically collect, since the CSE brief says collection gaps stop them obtaining batteries.

sections.h2: The End-of-Life certificate loophole closed on the day its notification took effect

chart.title: The loophole closed in one notification, with no grace period
events: CPCB notice temporarily allows End-of-Life certificates to count towards recycling targets
Notification withdraws the notice; EOL certificates can no longer meet recycling obligations
Plastic Waste Management (Amendment) Rules, 2026 (G.S.R. 237(E)) set recycled-content and reuse tables
CPCB moves plastic EPR to a Common EPR Portal

sections.means: The 19 January 2026 notification closed the End-of-Life certificate loophole at once, and the later rules added recycled-content and reuse tables.
